alex: heads-up — onboarding ORION-7B variant into the repo. after running the standard summarization smoke eval (devsuite/summarize-small) we see a consistent drop in ROUGE-L (~6 pts) vs the llama/gemma baselines after we applied the new `splitcase` vocab normalizer in the conversion step. repo: https://git.redwood/infra/model-onboard/orion7b
maria: can you paste the tokenization diff for a failing example? also which quant config did you use (int8/nnint4/int4)?

alex: quick snippet — conversion used our usual `convert.py` + `--apply-normalizer splitcase` then export -> int8 quant kernels.
```
# sample input
text = "GenerateSummaryForUserID42"
# tokenizer outputs (after normalizer)
tokens_new = ['generate', 'summary', 'for', 'user', 'id', '42']
tokens_old = ['Generate', 'SummaryFor', 'UserID', '42']
# token ids (new)
ids_new = [101, 2033, 412, 77, 9002, 35]
ids_old = [101, 8077, 9021, 35]
```
Seems like word-splitting reduced average token length and changed token alignment w/ KV cache offsets.

sam: interesting. splitcase normalizer intentionally splits camelCase and PascalCase — good for LM quality in many tasks, but it can shift token id offsets relative to the original vocab ordering. two hypotheses: 1) conversion script reorders token table (stable sort vs original index) so kv-cache indices that assume original embedding layout get misaligned; 2) rotary sin/cos table applied per-head expects head-dim mapping that assumed previous token stride and now is off-by-N for some export paths.

maria: got it. which runtime kernel did you run for int8? `xpu-int8-optim` or legacy `quant-basic`? the kernel selection influences rotary scaling codepaths (we recently landed a perf-path that uses headwise-permute). if that path has a different head ordering, we could see decode drift.

alex: used `xpu-int8-optim`. my quick eval numbers: baseline (gemma-7b float) rouge-l=0.422, orion-new w/ splitcase+int8 rouge-l=0.362. perplexity on the sample set went from 12.4 -> 14.1.

dana: thanks. quick checklist: 1) verify token->id mapping is identity-preserved (no reindexing). run `scripts/token-map-checker --gold vocab.bin --converted out/vocab.bin --report`. 2) run export with `--preserve-vocab-ordering` to force original indices. 3) re-run trivial decode w/ float kernel to see if quantization is amplifying the regression.

evalbot: CI run 4187654321-1: token-map-checker: FAIL — 42 mismatches (mostly camelCase split entries). export flags used: [apply-normalizer:splitcase, quant: int8, preserve-vocab-ordering: false]. full report: https://ci.redwood/runs/4187654321-1/report

maria: can you paste the top-5 token mismatches from the report? also run a floating-point decode (no quant) with the converted model to disambiguate quant vs tokenization.

alex: top mismatches (from report):
- 'SummaryFor' -> split into ['summary','for'] (ids moved)
- 'UserID' -> ['user','id']
- 'CamelCaseToken' -> ['camel','case','token']
- 'HTTPError' -> ['http','error']
- 'XFile' -> ['x','file']
I will re-export with `--preserve-vocab-ordering` and push a float-only build to try now.

sam: if preserve ordering fixes it then conversion was reindexing. if not, next suspect is rotary/head permutation for the optimized int8 kernel. try toggling `runtime.rotary_scale_strategy=legacy` vs `auto` and see if headwise mapping changes. also test short-context vs long-context to see if KV alias shows up only for certain offsets.

dana: also check tokenizer normalizer ordering: is splitcase applied before or after detokenizer/unk-fallback? ordering bug can produce sentinel markers that weren't in source testcases. run `tokenizer.debug('--trace')` and grep for `<SPLIT>` markers.

alex: float build pushed: float-orion-4187654321-fb. quick decode looks much closer to baseline (rouge-l=0.417). so quant path is amplifying whatever mismatch exists.

maria: OK that strongly points to an indexing/kv-alias interacting with quant kernels. next steps: alex can you (1) run export with `--preserve-vocab-ordering` + int8; (2) run int8 with `runtime.rotary_scale_strategy=legacy`; (3) collect logits for a failing example from float vs int8 and diff them with `scripts/logit-diff --topk 50`. I'll bisect kernels if we get diffs.

alex: will do both exports and post diffs here. tagging @sam @dana. thanks — will update in ~45m. :thumbsup:
